top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks are a mature, independently confirmed instrument achievement: magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms turned statistical power and systematic control into 10^-18 clocks that agree across laboratories and now test gravity, constants and dark matter. The credit is concentrated on Katori (proposal) and Ye (realisation and 10^-18 development), and the citation scope is narrow and accurate. As an experimentalist I value the patient calibration work behind it; no award is clearly weaker than this well-founded, consensus proposal.
